Details of prices of two items P and Q are presented in the above table. The ratio of cost of item P to cost of item Q is 3:4. Discount is calculated as the difference between the marked price and the selling price. The profit percentage is calculated as the ratio of the difference between selling price and cost, to the cost

$$\left(\text{Profit } \% = \frac{\text{Selling price}-\text{Cost}}{\text{Cost}} \times 100\right)$$

The discount on item Q, as a percentage of its marked price, is ________.
explanation:
Given Data:
• Cost price of item P, $\text{Cost}(P) = ₹ 5,400$
• Ratio of cost of item P to cost of item Q = $3:4$
• Profit % for item Q = $25\%$
• Marked Price of item Q, $\text{MP}(Q) = ₹ 10,000$

Step 1: Calculate the Cost Price of Item Q
$\frac{\text{Cost}(P)}{\text{Cost}(Q)} = \frac{3}{4}$
$\text{Cost}(Q) = \frac{4}{3} \times 5400 = ₹ 7,200$

Step 2: Calculate the Selling Price of Item Q
$\text{Profit } \% = \frac{\text{Selling Price} - \text{Cost}}{\text{Cost}} \times 100 = 25$
$\text{Selling Price}(Q) = 7200 + (0.25 \times 7200) = ₹ 9,000$

Step 3: Calculate Discount and Discount Percentage for Item Q
$\text{Discount} = \text{Marked Price} - \text{Selling Price} = 10000 - 9000 = ₹ 1,000$
$\text{Discount } \% = \left( \frac{\text{Discount}}{\text{Marked Price}} \right) \times 100 = \left( \frac{1000}{10000} \right) \times 100 = 10\%$

Thus, the correct option is C.
